entries.name: Caregiver
entries.summary: Brands that promise protection, comfort and generous help, expressed through soft warm palettes, rounded forms, human photography and calm, reassuring pacing.

entries.name: Creator
entries.summary: Brands that promise self-expression and the power to make things, expressed through distinctive custom type, paint-box color, tactile craft and visible process.

entries.name: Everyperson
entries.summary: Brands that promise belonging, honesty and fair value, expressed through friendly sans type, warm neutrals, real people and approachable, unpretentious design.

entries.name: Explorer
entries.summary: Brands that promise freedom, discovery and self-reliance, expressed through earthy palettes, big landscapes, rugged type and a sense of open horizon.

entries.name: Hero
entries.summary: Brands that prove worth through courage, discipline and mastery, expressed through high-contrast, forceful type, dynamic diagonals and decisive color.

entries.name: Innocent
entries.summary: Brands that promise simplicity, goodness and a fresh start, expressed through light, clean, friendly visuals and plain, optimistic language.

entries.name: Jester
entries.summary: Brands that promise fun, lightness and irreverence, expressed through saturated color, bouncy type, quirky illustration and spring-loaded motion.

entries.name: Lover
entries.summary: Brands that promise intimacy, beauty and passion, expressed through rich warm color, flowing curves, tactile close-ups and unhurried pacing.

entries.name: Magician
entries.summary: Brands that promise transformation and make the impossible feel possible, expressed through luminous color, depth, mystery and moments of reveal.

entries.name: Outlaw
entries.summary: Brands that break rules and reject the status quo, expressed through high-contrast black palettes, raw type, hard edges and confrontational voice.

entries.name: Ruler
entries.summary: Brands that promise control, order and prestige, expressed through disciplined grids, deep navy-black palettes, refined serifs and unhurried, symmetrical composition.

entries.name: Sage
entries.summary: Brands built on knowledge, insight and truth, expressed through calm structure, readable typography, evidence and restrained color.

entries.name: Affluent and High-Net-Worth
entries.summary: Time-poor, privacy-conscious and often 50+ clients who judge a brand by discretion, service and flawless execution; design for quiet confidence, human escalation, low friction and legible type.

entries.name: B2B Buying Committees
entries.summary: Groups of 6-10 stakeholders with different questions and risks; design evidence by role, shareable assets, transparent pricing and proof, and a journey that survives weeks of forwarding and silence.

entries.name: Children under 13
entries.summary: Young users with limited reading, fine-motor and abstract-reasoning skills; design for huge targets, audio and icons, forgiving flows and parent-gated commerce under strict child-privacy law.

entries.name: Disability and Accessibility-First
entries.summary: Products where people with vision, hearing, motor or cognitive disabilities are core users; treat WCAG 2.2 AA as the floor, build in keyboard, screen-reader and zoom support, and test with real users.

entries.name: Expert and Power Users
entries.summary: Daily professionals who value speed and depth over friendliness; give them dense layouts, keyboard-first control, saved views, bulk actions, undo and instant response, without losing accessibility.

entries.name: Low Bandwidth and Entry-Level Devices
entries.summary: Users on slow, metered networks and 1-3 GB RAM phones; design text-first pages under about 500 KB, 48px targets, 7:1 contrast, offline tolerance and honest data costs.

entries.name: Low Literacy / Plain Language
entries.summary: People who read slowly, in a second language or under stress; write at grade 5-6, show one step at a time, pair icons with words and never make comprehension a hurdle to a service.

entries.name: Neurodivergent Users
entries.summary: Users with ADHD, autism, dyslexia and related differences; reduce sensory load and surprises, support memory and executive function, keep language literal, and let people tune the interface.

entries.name: Older Adults (65+)
entries.summary: Adults 65+ with varied digital skill and age-related changes in vision, dexterity and memory; design for large text, 7:1 contrast, large targets, patient flows and a human support route.

entries.name: Teens and Gen Z
entries.summary: Phone-first 13-24 year olds who expect speed, expressive identity and peer-made content; designing for them now also means age assurance, privacy-by-default and no engagement dark patterns.

entries.name: E-commerce Store
entries.summary: Online stores where product imagery, price clarity, trust and a short path to checkout drive revenue; every screen is judged on add-to-cart and completed orders.

entries.name: Email
entries.summary: HTML email built for inconsistent clients (Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail) and dark mode, where a single column, tested code, one clear CTA and small file size beat visual ambition.

entries.name: Environmental Graphics and Wayfinding
entries.summary: Signs, maps and environmental graphics that guide people through buildings and sites; legibility at distance, decision-point placement, consistent naming and code compliance decide success.

entries.name: Marketing Website
entries.summary: Public websites that explain, persuade and convert; judged by clarity of message, speed, search visibility, accessibility and conversion rather than feature depth.

entries.name: Native Mobile App
entries.summary: iOS and Android apps designed to platform conventions, thumb reach, safe areas, gestures and store requirements; judged by speed, clarity and how native they feel.

entries.name: Out-of-Home and Digital Signage
entries.summary: Billboards, transit and digital screens read in seconds from distance; one idea, huge type, high contrast and ruthless copy cuts matter more than detail.

entries.name: Packaging
entries.summary: Three-dimensional, shelf-and-hand design where dielines, print process, barcodes, regulatory copy and material choice constrain a brand that must win in seconds.

entries.name: Presentations and Decks
entries.summary: Slides that support a speaker or a reader; 16:9 layouts with one message per slide, large type, strong templates and clear data stories beat dense documents on screen.

entries.name: Print Collateral
entries.summary: Printed pieces built for prepress from the start (bleed, CMYK, resolution, paper and finishing) where color and craft are judged in the hand at actual size.

entries.name: Social Media
entries.summary: Feed, story and short-video formats where a 1-3 second hook, platform-native framing and mobile-sized type decide whether anyone stops; specs change often.

entries.name: Video and Motion
entries.summary: Time-based work from brand films and ads to UI animation and social video, where aspect ratio, frame rate, codec, loudness and caption choices must be fixed before the first frame.

entries.name: Web Application
entries.summary: Logged-in browser products where speed, density, state handling and keyboard flow decide the experience; design for repeated daily tasks, not first impressions.

entries.name: AI Products
entries.summary: Assistants, copilots, agents and generative tools; trust is the design problem, so disclosure, sources, uncertainty and human control matter more than futuristic styling.

entries.name: Automotive and Mobility
entries.summary: Vehicles, dealer journeys and mobility services where emotion drives desire but safety rules govern the dashboard; design spans showroom, configurator, app and in-car interface.

entries.name: Beauty and Cosmetics
entries.summary: Skincare, makeup, hair and fragrance brands selling transformation and self-expression; texture, color accuracy, inclusive shade range and substantiated claims decide desire and trust.

entries.name: Creative Agencies and Studios
entries.summary: Businesses that sell creative judgment; their own site and identity are the portfolio, so craft, point of view and clear working process matter more than category conventions.

entries.name: Crypto and Web3
entries.summary: Exchanges, wallets, protocols and token communities; a category with reputational debt where credibility now depends on plain risk language, self-custody clarity and design restraint rather than hype.

entries.name: Developer Tools
entries.summary: Tools, APIs and platforms used by software engineers; credibility comes from documentation, speed and honest technical detail, and the brand is judged by how the docs and CLI feel.

entries.name: Digital Health and Wellness
entries.summary: Consumer health apps, telehealth brands, wearables and mental-health tools; caring and motivating, but handling sensitive data, avoiding medical overclaims and shame-driven patterns.

entries.name: E-commerce and DTC Retail
entries.summary: Brands that sell directly online; conversion depends on product imagery, speed, clear pricing and a frictionless checkout, while brand story differentiates in a market of look-alike storefronts.

entries.name: Education and EdTech
entries.summary: Schools, universities, learning platforms and training products; design must help people learn and persist, serve students, teachers and parents together, and protect minors' data and attention.

entries.name: Energy and Climate Tech
entries.summary: Utilities, renewables and climate tech where trust rests on verifiable claims and clear bills; green aesthetics are saturated, so evidence, data and honest tone are the differentiators.

entries.name: Events and Conferences
entries.summary: Time-boxed gatherings sold on programme, people and atmosphere; the identity must work across site, ticket, badge, stage and signage, with price transparency and access information up front.

entries.name: Fashion and Apparel
entries.summary: Clothing, footwear and accessories sold on identity and desire; image, typography and editorial voice carry the brand while fit, returns and sustainability claims decide trust.

entries.name: Fintech and Banking
entries.summary: Money products where trust, clarity and control come first; differentiation now comes from tone, craft and transparency rather than blue-and-shield symbolism.

entries.name: Food, Beverage and CPG
entries.summary: Packaged food, drink and household goods sold through shelves, shops and screens; shelf impact, label compliance, appetite appeal and everyday trust all converge on the pack.

entries.name: Gaming and Esports
entries.summary: Interactive entertainment and competitive scenes where community, identity and in-game UI matter as much as key art; rules on ratings, loot boxes and minors shape monetization design.

entries.name: Government and Civic
entries.summary: Public services used by everyone, often under stress and without a choice; success is task completion, plain language, accessibility and earned trust rather than brand expression.

entries.name: Healthcare Providers
entries.summary: Hospitals, clinics and practices where patients arrive anxious and in a hurry; design must make finding care, booking, paying and understanding results calm, accessible and private.

entries.name: Hotels and Travel
entries.summary: Hotels, airlines, booking platforms and destinations selling trips and stays; imagery sells desire, but date pickers, total prices, maps and trustworthy itineraries decide the booking.

entries.name: Industrial, Manufacturing and Construction
entries.summary: Physical, safety-critical and spec-driven B2B categories where buyers want proof, uptime and clear information; design earns trust through precision, durability and plain engineering language.

entries.name: Insurance
entries.summary: Products sold on the promise of protection when things go wrong; design must make complex coverage understandable, quotes fast and claims humane while staying within heavily regulated disclosures.

entries.name: Kids and Family
entries.summary: Products for children and the adults who buy and supervise them; two audiences, strict privacy and advertising law, and a design bar set by safety, comprehension and parent trust.

entries.name: Legal and Professional Services
entries.summary: Expertise sold on reputation and judgment; clients buy credibility, clarity and a named person, within advertising and confidentiality rules that limit how bold the brand can be.

entries.name: Logistics and Supply Chain
entries.summary: Moving goods reliably across modes and borders; brands win on dependable tracking, exception handling and operator-grade tools, within strict labeling, safety and customs conventions.

entries.name: Luxury Goods
entries.summary: Scarce, crafted goods sold on heritage, desire and discretion; design is restraint, material truth and service, with legal attention to origin, materials and sustainability claims.

entries.name: Marketplaces and Platforms
entries.summary: Two-sided products that must earn trust between strangers; design balances supply and demand, makes quality and safety legible, and now operates under platform-specific transparency laws.

entries.name: Media, Entertainment and Streaming
entries.summary: Content businesses where artwork, discovery and playback carry the brand; the interface must disappear behind the title while meeting accessibility, ratings and subscription rules.

entries.name: Nonprofits and NGOs
entries.summary: Mission-driven organizations that must earn donor trust, protect the dignity of the people they serve and prove impact; design is judged by transparency and restraint as much as emotion.

entries.name: Pharma and Biotech
entries.summary: Prescription and OTC medicines, biotech platforms and medical devices; communication is shaped by fair-balance rules, scientific evidence and patient need, so clarity of risk is part of the design.

entries.name: Real Estate and PropTech
entries.summary: Brokerages, listing portals, developers and property technology; often the largest purchase of a life, so trust, local knowledge, honest imagery and fair-housing rules shape every screen.

entries.name: Restaurants and Food Service
entries.summary: Restaurants, cafes, bars and delivery brands where appetite, atmosphere and convenience meet; menus, signage, ordering flows and reservations carry the brand through every touchpoint.

entries.name: B2B SaaS
entries.summary: Subscription software sold to teams and companies; buyers weigh proof, security and time-to-value, so the product itself is the hero and brand is expressed through craft, point of view and clarity.

entries.name: Sports and Fitness
entries.summary: Performance, community and identity products, from teams and sportswear to gyms and training apps; energy and motivation sell, while body image, health data and subscriptions need care.

entries.name: Australia and New Zealand
entries.summary: English-language Pacific markets with a relaxed tone, tap-to-pay and BNPL habits, Indigenous protocols (First Nations, te reo Māori), GST-inclusive prices and strong consumer and privacy law.

entries.name: Brazil
entries.summary: Portuguese-speaking, mobile-first market where Pix, boleto and card installments shape checkout, LGPD and consumer code rules apply, and WhatsApp is the default channel.

entries.name: Canada
entries.summary: Officially bilingual (English and French) North American market where Quebec French law, Canadian spelling, Interac payments and accessibility statutes shape design.

entries.name: Mainland China
entries.summary: Simplified-Chinese mobile super-app market where WeChat, Alipay and Douyin dominate, info-dense interfaces are normal, and PIPL, ICP licensing and ad-law rules shape design and hosting.

entries.name: DACH and the Nordics
entries.summary: High-trust, high-income markets where precision, privacy, strict consumer law, bank-based digital ID (BankID, MitID) and mobile payments (Swish, Vipps, TWINT) define design.

entries.name: India and South Asia
entries.summary: Android-first, multilingual and multi-script region where UPI, WhatsApp and vernacular interfaces drive adoption, with Indic-script typesetting, lakh/crore numbers and new DPDP privacy rules.

entries.name: Israel (Hebrew)
entries.summary: Hebrew right-to-left market with a tech-savvy, direct, mobile-first audience, Hebrew-Arabic-Russian-English multilingualism, installment-heavy payments and Shabbat and holiday rhythms.

entries.name: Japan
entries.summary: Japanese-language market with three scripts, polite register, information-rich layouts, iPhone-heavy mobile use, LINE, PayPay, konbini payments and tax-inclusive pricing under APPI and commerce law.

entries.name: South Korea
entries.summary: Hangul-script, hyper-connected mobile market where KakaoTalk, Naver and Toss lead, Samsung devices dominate, trends move fast, and PIPA consent rules are among the strictest in Asia.

entries.name: Spanish-speaking Latin America
entries.summary: Mobile-first Spanish-speaking region from Mexico to Argentina with diverse dialects, cash-and-voucher payments, instant bank transfers, wallets and a fast-changing patchwork of data laws.

entries.name: Middle East and North Africa (Arabic)
entries.summary: Right-to-left Arabic-script markets from the Gulf to the Maghreb, mobile-first and young, with strong religious and family norms, mada and cash-on-delivery payments, and fast-evolving data laws.

entries.name: Southeast Asia
entries.summary: Mobile-first, young, multilingual region (Latin, Thai, Khmer, Lao, Burmese scripts) where super apps, QR wallets, cash on delivery and messaging commerce shape design; laws differ by country.

entries.name: Sub-Saharan Africa
entries.summary: Young, mobile-money-led, multilingual region with low-end Android, costly data and USSD reach; Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Ghana lead digital adoption, with fast-growing data laws.

entries.name: United Kingdom and Ireland
entries.summary: English-language British and Irish markets with distinct spelling, GBP versus EUR, strong plain-language and accessibility traditions, UK GDPR/PECR and EU GDPR, and bilingual Welsh and Irish duties.

entries.name: United States
entries.summary: Large, diverse English-first market with Spanish as a major second language; shaped by card and wallet payments, a patchwork of state privacy laws, and ADA accessibility litigation.

entries.name: US Hispanic, Puerto Rico and the Caribbean
entries.summary: Bilingual English/Spanish design for US Hispanic and Latino audiences, Puerto Rico (a US territory with Spanish dominant) and Caribbean markets; varied origins, Spanish variants and payments.

entries.name: Western Europe (France, Iberia, Italy, Benelux)
entries.summary: Multilingual EU markets with strict GDPR cookie rules, the European Accessibility Act, national payment schemes (iDEAL, Bizum, Carte Bancaire, Multibanco) and local language laws.

entries.name: Art Deco
entries.summary: Symmetrical geometric glamour - gold on black, sunbursts, chevrons and stepped forms, tall display capitals and lacquered, machine-age luxury from the Jazz Age.

entries.name: Art Nouveau and Ornamental
entries.summary: Flowing whiplash curves, botanical ornament, arched frames and hand-lettered display type in muted natural colors; decoration fused with structure, c. 1890-1910.

entries.name: Bauhaus and Constructivist
entries.summary: Primary-color geometry, circles-squares-triangles, bold sans type and diagonal composition; form follows function, with Constructivism adding agitprop energy and photomontage.

entries.name: Bold Geometric / Sport Energy
entries.summary: Heavy condensed type, diagonal geometry, hard color blocks and oversized numerals that convey speed, power and competition; built for sport, fitness, events and performance brands.

entries.name: Civic Plain / Public Service
entries.summary: Task-first public-service design with plain language, large readable type, high contrast, strong focus states and proven patterns, as in the GOV.UK Design System and the US Web Design System.

entries.name: Classic Luxury Serif
entries.summary: Centered, ceremonial heritage luxury - light serif or Roman capitals, deep jewel grounds with antique gold, hairline rules, slow fades and abundant space; price signaled through restraint.

entries.name: Clinical Calm
entries.summary: Reassuring healthcare clarity with soft teal-blue, warm neutrals, plain language, large targets and low-stimulation layouts that lower anxiety and prevent errors without feeling sterile.

entries.name: Collage / Mixed Media
entries.summary: Layered cut-out photography, paper scraps, tape, halftone and mixed type arranged with deliberate tension; handmade, surprising and culturally literate, but easy to turn into scrapbook noise.

entries.name: Corporate Modern / Enterprise Clean
entries.summary: Credible, systematized business design with one deep brand blue, cool neutrals, modular cards, restrained 6-8px radius and product-led imagery; trust through consistency rather than flair.

entries.name: Dark Tech / Developer
entries.summary: Near-black canvas, hairline borders, monospace accents and one signal color; built for people who live in terminals and editors, with code and real product output as the hero visual.

entries.name: Data-Dense / Utilitarian
entries.summary: Maximum information per screen for expert users, with tabular figures, small type, tight rows, semantic color only, keyboard control and tiled panels, as in trading terminals and ops tools.

entries.name: Eco / Natural / Sustainable
entries.summary: Earth-tone palettes, warm serifs, organic shapes and honest material and process imagery that signal care for people and planet, backed by specific proof rather than green decoration.

entries.name: Editorial / Magazine
entries.summary: Publication-grade hierarchy - high-contrast serif display, readable text serif, multi-column grids, pull quotes, strong crops and one spot color; design that makes reading feel curated.

entries.name: Fashion Editorial / Didone
entries.summary: High-contrast Didone display type, vast white space, full-bleed fashion photography and hairline rules, in the lineage of Harper's Bazaar and Vogue; luxury through restraint, scale and crop.

entries.name: Flat / Material
entries.summary: Color-field, ornament-free flat design plus Google's Material system with tonal color, state layers, tiered elevation and spring motion; a predictable, highly implementable look for apps and tools.

entries.name: Glass and Spatial UI
entries.summary: Translucent, layered interfaces from glassmorphism to visionOS glass and Apple's 2025 Liquid Glass; blur, light and depth build hierarchy, but legibility rules decide whether it works.

entries.name: Grunge / Punk / DIY Zine
entries.summary: Photocopied, cut-and-paste, hand-made graphics - ransom-note lettering, torn paper, tape, marker scrawl, black-and-white with fluorescent hits; urgency, authenticity and refusal of polish.

entries.name: Handcrafted / Organic
entries.summary: Warm, imperfect and human-made - hand-drawn lines, soft wobbly shapes, earthy dyes, paper and linen textures and a friendly soft serif; the maker's hand is visible and trusted.

entries.name: Illustrative / Narrative
entries.summary: Illustration carries the story and the brand through a consistent hand-made world of characters, scenes and lettering on warm paper tones, with type and layout supporting the narrative.

entries.name: Kinetic / Experimental Typography
entries.summary: Letterforms as the main image and behavior, using variable-font axes, scale extremes and motion that respond to scroll, pointer or sound, with a readable resting state and disciplined limits.

entries.name: Maximalist / Eclectic
entries.summary: Controlled abundance - jewel colors, clashing patterns, layered type and imagery, mixed eras and shapes, held together by one repeated device; richness, humor and personality over restraint.

entries.name: Memphis / Postmodern
entries.summary: Playful 1980s postmodern geometry - squiggles, zigzags, confetti and terrazzo patterns, pastel-and-primary clashes, tilted shapes and wide geometric type; deliberate bad taste made joyful.

entries.name: Mid-Century Modern
entries.summary: Optimistic postwar modernism - organic and geometric shapes, cut-paper illustration, warm walnut, teal and burnt-orange palettes, and friendly gothic and slab type from c. 1945-1969.

entries.name: Neo-Brutalism
entries.summary: Friendly, loud interfaces - thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat pastel and saturated fills, chunky grotesque type and snappy press states; playful structure, still highly legible.

entries.name: Playful / Bubbly
entries.summary: Round, chunky, saturated and bouncy, with pill buttons, blob shapes, mascots and springy motion that make products feel friendly and easy, provided contrast and seriousness are managed.

entries.name: Quiet Minimal / Japandi
entries.summary: Calm, warm minimalism - low-chroma paper and stone tones, soft mincho or gentle sans type, vast negative space and near-still motion; emptiness is the feature, not the absence of one.

entries.name: Retro-Futurism / Synthwave
entries.summary: The 1980s imagining the future - neon magenta and cyan on deep violet, sunset gradients, perspective grids, chrome-and-italic type and scanlines; nostalgic night-drive energy with a space-age lineage.

entries.name: Risograph / Print Texture
entries.summary: Limited fluorescent and spot inks overprinted on uncoated paper with grain, halftone and slight misregistration; a tactile, indie-print look that works best when built from real ink separations.

entries.name: Scandinavian / Nordic
entries.summary: Light, functional and friendly - pale grounds, birch and fjord tones, humanist sans with a soft serif, rounded but restrained shapes and practical clarity; design for everyday life.

entries.name: 70s Psychedelic / Groovy
entries.summary: Warm, curvy 1960s-70s optimism - fat soft serifs, wavy bands, sunbursts and concentric arcs in avocado, harvest gold, burnt orange and plum; sensual, sunny and a little trippy.

entries.name: Skeuomorphic / Tactile
entries.summary: Interfaces modeled on real materials and devices (leather, brass, felt, knobs, switches) with consistent top lighting, bevels and texture so controls explain themselves by looking physical.

entries.name: Soft UI / Neumorphism
entries.summary: Monochrome surfaces extruded or pressed with paired light and dark shadows; tactile and calm, but a frequent AI default with weak contrast and affordance unless engineered carefully.

entries.name: Swiss / International Typographic Style
entries.summary: Objective, grid-driven design with asymmetric layouts, grotesque sans-serif type, flat color and photography; clarity itself is the aesthetic.

entries.name: Vibrant Gradient / Aurora SaaS
entries.summary: Luminous mesh or aurora gradients behind clean product UI to signal energy and innovation; a very common SaaS and AI default that needs controlled hues, solid text surfaces and a distinctive concept.

entries.name: Vintage Heritage / Americana
entries.summary: Turn-of-the-century to mid-century American print craft - wood-type slabs, badges and banners, letterpress ink, cream paper and barn-red, navy and mustard; authenticity from specific, earned detail.

entries.name: Raw Web Brutalism
entries.summary: Deliberately raw websites - system fonts, browser-blue links, hard black-and-white blocks and visible structure; honesty and speed over polish. Niche and risky; needs usability scaffolding.

entries.name: Y2K / Cyber
entries.summary: Millennium-era techno-optimism - glossy aqua buttons, chrome and bubble forms, sci-fi extended type, translucent panels and acid accents on icy or void grounds; nostalgic, glossy, energetic.

entries.name: Luxury
entries.summary: Desire, heritage and craft over features; dramatic negative space, high-contrast serif type, black-ivory-metal palettes, slow motion and ceremonial packaging, with price withheld or understated.

entries.name: Mid-Market
entries.summary: The reliable, friendly, worth-it middle; clear benefits, humanist type, soft corners, warm photography and proof of quality, with a distinct personality so the brand is not squeezed between tiers.

entries.name: Premium
entries.summary: Quality made visible; restrained palettes, refined type, generous space and tactile materials let evidence of craft, ingredients and expertise justify a higher price without luxury theatrics.

entries.name: Ultra-Luxury / Bespoke
entries.summary: Discretion over display; near-silent layouts, material-true palettes, small calm type, no prices or promotions and access by relationship, so the work and the service speak instead of the logo.

entries.name: Value / Mass Market
entries.summary: Price is the hero; the design signals savings, clarity and speed with loud color, heavy sans type, big numerals and dense, honest layouts that stay disciplined rather than cheap-looking.
